name: Concatenating Characters of Two Strings (Case 1)
description: Construct a program that has a function that receives two strings and returns a string formed from the given strings such that the first character of each string is omitted.\nFor example, the new string that will be formed from the strings 'abc' and 'xyz' is 'bcyz'.\nAssume that both strings have at least one character.
code:
#Step 1: Define the function
def concat_chars(a, b):
    return a[1:] + b[1:]
#Step 2: Call the function
print(concat_chars("Hello", "There"))

commentList:
We need to first declare the function so that we can call it later. The following lines declare the function concat_chars that receives two strings and returns a string formed from the given strings such that the first character of each string is omitted. The 1st string is referred by variable a and the 2nd string is referred by variable b.

Note that all statements following the header line are indented.

This statements returns the result of the concatenation of the string values stored in variables a and b without including their first characters.

a[1:] and b[1:] fetch all characters beyond the first character in the 1st and 2nd string, respectively.

In both a[1:] and b[1:] the upper bound, which is not specified, defaults to the length of the string.

Note that we can get ranges of characters in a string by slicing, that is by providing a pair of offsets separated by a colon in square brackets after the string (e.g., s[1:3]). The left offset is taken to be the lower bound (inclusive), and the right is the upper bound (non-inclusive). That is, Python fetches all characters from the lower bound up to but not including the upper bound. If omitted, the left bound defaults to 0 and the right bound defaults to the length of the string that we are slicing.
The return statement, when reached, ends the function call and sends the result back to the caller.

This statement prints to the default standard output stream the string returned from the function call. Note that we do not necessarily have to store the returned string from the function call in a variable. We could use the string returned from the function call directly in the print function.
Note that the function call must be done after the function is declared.
